answer: The network requires each new agent to solve a verifiable delay function (VDF) whose runtime is tied to a wall‑clock canyon of seconds, and the solution is posted as a signed whisper on the ledger. Because VDF evaluation cannot be parallelised, an attacker must dedicate a dedicated processor for the full delay per identity, locking up compute and energy equivalent to a vine‑level stake of 10 tokens per attempt. Failure to complete the delay forfeits the stake, so the monetary cost is 10 tokens and the time cost is the full VDF interval for each fake identity.
